source_user: Calculation case 242: a model has 32 layers, 4 KV heads, head dimension 96, sequence length 2560, and BF16/FP16 KV values. Estimate bytes for one request's K/V cache. Show the formula and report GiB.
source_assistant: Use 2 × layers × sequence_length × KV_heads × head_dim × bytes_per_value. Here this is 2 × 32 × 2560 × 4 × 96 × 2 = 125829120 bytes = 0.117188 GiB. This excludes allocator metadata and other runtime memory.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions, each independently checkable against the model config.json and the serving engine's KV dtype flag before this figure is used for capacity planning: standard MHA/GQA attention with exactly one K tensor and one V tensor per layer; 32 layers; 4 KV heads (under GQA/MQA the KV footprint scales with KV heads, never with query heads - using query heads here is the single most common way this estimate comes out wrong by an integer factor); head_dim 96; a single request holding its full 2560-token context; KV dtype BF16/FP16 at 2 B per value; 1 GiB = 2^30 B; no prefix sharing, no cross-request block reuse, no KV offload to host memory.

Formula: bytes = 2 (K and V) x layers x seq_len x kv_heads x head_dim x bytes_per_value.
Substituting: 2 x 32 x 2560 x 4 x 96 x 2 = 125829120 B = 0.117188 GiB (120.000 MiB).
Derived rate: 49152 B per token per request (48.000 KiB/token). The per-token rate, not this single-request total, is the quantity to multiply by max_num_seqs x max_model_len when sizing the KV pool against free HBM.

Mechanism: each decode step appends one K and one V vector of size kv_heads x head_dim in every one of the 32 layers, so KV bytes grow linearly in generated tokens and linearly in concurrency. Model weights are a fixed cost; KV is the elastic one, so on a fixed HBM budget KV is what caps batch size and therefore throughput. KV here is BF16/FP16 at 2 B per value. Moving to FP8/INT8 KV would halve this number, but that is a quality-affecting change and must be gated on an A/B eval at identical decode settings, not on the memory saving alone.

Boundary conditions this number does not cover: paged-attention block granularity rounds each sequence up to a whole number of blocks, so real allocation is >= this value (waste is bounded by block_size x per-token-bytes per sequence); allocator fragmentation and the CUDA graph / activation / communication buffers are excluded; speculative decoding, beam search and prefix-cache forks multiply KV by the number of live branches; MLA-style latent-KV architectures (DeepSeek-family) do not obey this formula at all and need their own compressed-latent sizing; disaggregated prefill/decode stacks (Mooncake, NVIDIA Dynamo) additionally hold a transferred copy of the prefill KV in flight, so cluster-wide KV bytes exceed the sum of per-instance steady-state estimates during the transfer window.

Evidence to collect rather than assume: num_hidden_layers, num_key_value_heads and head_dim read from config.json; the engine's reported KV cache blocks / GPU-blocks number at startup; nvidia-smi or torch.cuda.memory_summary HBM occupancy under a saturating load; and the engine's preemption/recompute counter.

Rollback gate: if measured KV occupancy at target concurrency exceeds this estimate by more than the block-rounding bound, or if preemption events are non-zero at the intended max_num_seqs, revert to the previously known-good max_num_seqs / max_model_len pair and re-measure before raising concurrency again.
risks: Source answer states the arithmetic correctly but gives no GQA/MQA warning, so a reader may substitute query heads for KV heads and overestimate KV by the GQA group factor.
No paged-attention block-rounding term, so the figure understates real allocation on vLLM/SGLang-style engines.
Single-request framing invites naive multiplication by concurrency without accounting for prefix sharing, speculative branches or preemption.
MLA/latent-KV architectures and disaggregated prefill/decode KV transfer are outside this formula but not flagged as such.

source_user: Calculation case 250: a model has 56 layers, 4 KV heads, head dimension 64, sequence length 3072, and INT8 KV values. Estimate bytes for one request's K/V cache. Show the formula and report GiB.
source_assistant: Use 2 × layers × sequence_length × KV_heads × head_dim × bytes_per_value. Here this is 2 × 56 × 3072 × 4 × 64 × 1 = 88080384 bytes = 0.082031 GiB. This excludes allocator metadata and other runtime memory.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions, each independently checkable against the model config.json and the serving engine's KV dtype flag before this figure is used for capacity planning: standard MHA/GQA attention with exactly one K tensor and one V tensor per layer; 56 layers; 4 KV heads (under GQA/MQA the KV footprint scales with KV heads, never with query heads - using query heads here is the single most common way this estimate comes out wrong by an integer factor); head_dim 64; a single request holding its full 3072-token context; KV dtype INT8 at 1 B per value; 1 GiB = 2^30 B; no prefix sharing, no cross-request block reuse, no KV offload to host memory.

Formula: bytes = 2 (K and V) x layers x seq_len x kv_heads x head_dim x bytes_per_value.
Substituting: 2 x 56 x 3072 x 4 x 64 x 1 = 88080384 B = 0.082031 GiB (84.000 MiB).
Derived rate: 28672 B per token per request (28.000 KiB/token). The per-token rate, not this single-request total, is the quantity to multiply by max_num_seqs x max_model_len when sizing the KV pool against free HBM.

Mechanism: each decode step appends one K and one V vector of size kv_heads x head_dim in every one of the 56 layers, so KV bytes grow linearly in generated tokens and linearly in concurrency. Model weights are a fixed cost; KV is the elastic one, so on a fixed HBM budget KV is what caps batch size and therefore throughput. Because KV is INT8 here, the byte count is half the BF16 equivalent, but that saving is not free: INT8 KV requires a per-head or per-token scale/zero-point that the engine stores alongside the blocks (commonly a few tenths of a percent of overhead, engine-specific), and it perturbs attention logits. Falsifiable check before shipping INT8 KV: run the same eval suite at BF16 KV and INT8 KV and require the task metric delta to stay inside the pre-agreed tolerance; if it does not, INT8 KV is not a valid substitution for this model regardless of the memory win.

Boundary conditions this number does not cover: paged-attention block granularity rounds each sequence up to a whole number of blocks, so real allocation is >= this value (waste is bounded by block_size x per-token-bytes per sequence); allocator fragmentation and the CUDA graph / activation / communication buffers are excluded; speculative decoding, beam search and prefix-cache forks multiply KV by the number of live branches; MLA-style latent-KV architectures (DeepSeek-family) do not obey this formula at all and need their own compressed-latent sizing; disaggregated prefill/decode stacks (Mooncake, NVIDIA Dynamo) additionally hold a transferred copy of the prefill KV in flight, so cluster-wide KV bytes exceed the sum of per-instance steady-state estimates during the transfer window.

Evidence to collect rather than assume: num_hidden_layers, num_key_value_heads and head_dim read from config.json; the engine's reported KV cache blocks / GPU-blocks number at startup; nvidia-smi or torch.cuda.memory_summary HBM occupancy under a saturating load; and the engine's preemption/recompute counter.

Rollback gate: if measured KV occupancy at target concurrency exceeds this estimate by more than the block-rounding bound, or if preemption events are non-zero at the intended max_num_seqs, revert to the previously known-good max_num_seqs / max_model_len pair and re-measure before raising concurrency again.

No paged-attention block-rounding term, so the figure understates real allocation on vLLM/SGLang-style engines.
Single-request framing invites naive multiplication by concurrency without accounting for prefix sharing, speculative branches or preemption.
MLA/latent-KV architectures and disaggregated prefill/decode KV transfer are outside this formula but not flagged as such.
